subject: economics
title: Regulation and Permits
welcome_lead: When prices alone are not enough - rules and tradable permits step.
meta_desc: A-Level Government Intervention: regulation, public provision, permits.
final_note: Quantity controls suit pollution; subsidies suit positive externalities.

concepts.def: Right to emit a fixed amount, freely traded.
Intervention that creates worse outcomes than the market.

walkthroughs.body_html: Regulation suits cases where exact behaviour matters - safety standards, drug approvals - or where prices cannot capture the externality cleanly.
Cap-and-trade sets a total cap and lets firms trade permits. Efficient cuts happen where they are cheapest. The EU ETS and California ETS are working examples.
Bad intervention is worse than none - regulatory capture, unintended consequences, information gaps and bureaucracy can all make matters worse.

options: Cap total emissions and let firms trade permits
Intervention leads to worse outcomes than the market
